A group of crows is called a murder.

The text provided contains a classic social engineering tactic known as a Business Email Compromise (BEC) or spear-phishing attack. The attacker impersonates a high-ranking executive (the CEO) to create a sense of urgency and authority, which pressures employees to bypass standard security protocols. By claiming that immediate action is required to "prevent data loss" and instructing staff to send sensitive customer data to an external email for "safekeeping," the attacker attempts to trick employees into exfiltrating confidential information. This relies on manipulating fear of data loss and the expectation of compliance with executive orders.
